content: The current emission state is a pause that began 14.8 days ago when episode 42 ended on 2026-02-15 [E5]. At Pahala, the maximum 24‑hour SO2 concentration over the last day was 26.3 ppb, the mean was 2.7 ppb, and the latest reading at 16:00 HST was 0.2 ppb [E1]; the upwind Volcanoes NP station shows no data, with a maximum of 0.0 ppb and a mean of -0.1 ppb [E3]. Forecast transport indicates that 1 of 3 925 hPa leads are directed toward Pahala with a mean component of 3.3 m/s toward the station, while 850 hPa winds at the summit are 4.7 m/s from 35 deg and 6.1 m/s from 19 deg at 00:00 HST [E6]. The stability profile shows a boundary layer that collapses from 443 m at 18:00 HST to 127 m by 06:00 HST, capped by an inversion base at 2193 m [E7], which limits vertical mixing during the overnight period.
